Choose the random-walk orders of a Bayesian APC model by DIC

Source: R/model-apc_bayes.R
apc_select.Rd

Fits apc_bayes() with every combination of first- and second-order random walks for age, period and cohort (and, optionally, with and without overdispersion) and ranks the variants by the deviance information criterion (Spiegelhalter et al. 2002) that bamp reports, summed over strata. DIC measures in-sample fit; to choose by forecast accuracy, compare the candidates with mt_backtest() instead. Selection on all data followed by a backtest of the selected model reuses the test years once.

Usage

apc_select(
  data,
  prep = NULL,
  orders = c("rw1", "rw2"),
  overdispersion = FALSE,
  mcmc = mcmc_control("fast"),
  ...
)

Arguments

data

An mt_data object.

prep

Optional mt_prep() pipeline.

orders

Random-walk orders to try.

overdispersion

Values of overdispersion to try.

mcmc

MCMC settings, see mcmc_control().

...

Further arguments of apc_bayes().

Value

A list of class mt_apc_selection with best (the chosen specification) and table (DIC, effective number of parameters pd and deviance at the posterior mean per candidate, sorted by DIC; DIC = deviance at the mean + 2 pd).

References

Spiegelhalter DJ, Best NG, Carlin BP, van der Linde A (2002). Bayesian measures of model complexity and fit. Journal of the Royal Statistical Society B 64(4): 583-639.

Examples

# \donttest{
if (requireNamespace("bamp", quietly = TRUE)) {
  x <- mt_example(years = 2005:2019)
  sel <- apc_select(x, prep = mt_prep(step_ungroup()), orders = "rw1", mcmc = mcmc_control("test"))
  sel$table
}
#>       age period cohort overdispersion      dic      pd deviance_at_mean
#>    <char> <char> <char>         <lgcl>    <num>   <num>            <num>
#> 1:    rw1    rw1    rw1          FALSE 1028.362 130.922         766.5181
#>    converged
#>       <lgcl>
#> 1:      TRUE
# }
